title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 215 (Right of principal when agent deals, on his own account, in business of agency without principal’s consent)

content.overview: If an agent deals on his own account in the business of the agency, without first obtaining the consent of his principal and acquainting him with all material circumstances which have come to his own knowledge on the subject, the principal may repudiate the transaction if the case shows either that any material fact has been dishonestly concealed from him by the agent, or that the dealings of the agent have been disadvantageous to him.
content.glance: Own-account dealing without consent and full disclosure → principal may repudiate if dishonest concealment or disadvantageous dealing.
content.study: If an agent deals on his own account in the business of the agency, without first obtaining the consent of his principal and acquainting him with all material circumstances which have come to his own knowledge on the subject, the principal may repudiate the transaction if the case shows either that any material fact has been dishonestly concealed from him by the agent, or that the dealings of the agent have been disadvantageous to him. Connected: s. 216 (claim benefit from undisclosed own-account dealing).

sections.heading: Own-account dealing without consent and disclosure
sections.body: Agent deals on own account without consent and without acquainting principal with all material circumstances.

sections.heading: Grounds for repudiation
sections.body: Dishonest concealment of material fact, or dealings disadvantageous to the principal.

provisions.title: Right of principal when agent deals, on his own account, in business of agency without principal’s consent

examples.title: Application of Section 215
examples.body: Facts that satisfy the elements stated in the statutory text of Section 215 produce the consequence described in that section. Do not add elements beyond the text.

hypotheticals.question: Do the facts engage Section 215?
hypotheticals.analysis: Compare the facts with the statutory elements in Section 215. If they match, the statutory consequence follows; otherwise it does not.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 215 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Show own-account dealing without consent and full disclosure; test dishonest concealment or disadvantage; conclude on repudiation.
